raw_case_text:
A 75-year-old Saudi male farmer with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a 3-month progressive neurological decline. Initial symptoms included impaired hand coordination and task sequencing, followed by visual and auditory hallucinations. A short febrile illness with vomiting ensued, after which he developed cachexia, postural instability, frequent falls, bradykinesia, bilateral tremors, hypophonia, incontinence, and cognitive deterioration.
He denied recent travel or consumption of unpasteurized dairy products but had over 20 years of close contact with cattle, goats, and sheep.
Neurologic examination revealed inattention, non-fluent aphasia, impaired recall (MoCA 9/26), bilateral resting and kinetic tremors, lower limb rigidity, bradykinesia, and reduced strength (Medical Research Council (MRC) 3/5 right side, 2/5 left side). Hyperreflexia was present. Full sensory and cerebellar assessment was limited by his attentional deficits.
Routine labs were unremarkable except for an elevated HbA1c. Brucella serology was strongly positive (>1:1280), and thyroid peroxidase antibodies were also elevated. Although Brucella species could not be isolated by culture, the diagnosis was supported by serology and confirmed by a positive CSF Brucella PCR. An initial cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed elevated protein (2.97 g/L) and mild pleocytosis (12 WBCs/mm3, 75% lymphocytes). A second lumbar puncture, performed approximately 2 weeks later, revealed turbid CSF, increased WBCs (14/mm3, 70% neutrophils), higher protein (3.37 g/L), and a slightly low glucose (4.6 mmol/L).
An initial brain MRI showed right temporal cortical lesions, acute frontoparietal lacunar infarcts, background microangiopathy, and atrophy. A second MRI, obtained 2 weeks later, demonstrated diffuse pachymeningeal and leptomeningeal enhancement (Figure 1). A third MRI, done about 2 months later, showed persistent pachymeningeal enhancement and a new focal lesion in the left temporal convexity, without acute ischemia.
He was started on a combination antibiotic regimen consisting of oral doxycycline (100 mg twice daily), oral rifampin (600 mg once daily), oral sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (800/160 mg twice daily), and intravenous ceftriaxone (2 g once daily, administered intermittently). This initial course continued for approximately 2.5 months. Due to persistently elevated CSF protein levels despite clinical and radiologic improvement, a second antibiotic course of the same oral regimen (doxycycline, rifampin, and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim) was administered for an additional 6 weeks. Corticosteroids (oral dexamethasone 4 mg every 6 h) were given concurrently during the first month and then tapered over 3 weeks in response to persistent imaging abnormalities.
CSF Brucella PCR became negative, and serological titers declined to 1:640, indicating microbiological response.
The patient's clinical condition improved substantially, with resolution of hallucinations, bradykinesia, and rigidity. Strength improved to 4/5 in all limbs, though mild kinetic tremor and urinary symptoms persisted. He completed a 2-month rehabilitation program and was subsequently discharged home.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 75-year-old Saudi male farmer presented with a 3-month history of progressive cognitive decline, visual and auditory hallucinations, parkinsonism, and recurrent falls.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 75-year-old male farmer developed impaired hand coordination and task sequencing 3 months prior to presentation, rapidly followed by visual and auditory hallucinations and a brief febrile illness with vomiting. Thereafter, he experienced progressive cachexia, postural instability with frequent falls, bradykinesia, bilateral resting and kinetic tremors, hypophonia, urinary incontinence, and severe cognitive deterioration.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; over 20 years of close occupational contact with cattle, goats, and sheep as a farmer. Denied recent travel or consumption of unpasteurized dairy products.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for cognitive decline, visual and auditory hallucinations, transient fever and vomiting, weight loss/cachexia, gait instability, falls, tremor, slowness of movement, hypophonia, and urinary incontinence.

objective.physical_examination: Inattentive with non-fluent aphasia and severely impaired recall (MoCA score 9/26). Bilateral resting and kinetic tremors, lower extremity rigidity, generalized bradykinesia, asymmetric motor weakness (MRC grade 3/5 on the right, 2/5 on the left), and generalized hyperreflexia.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine hematologic and metabolic panels unremarkable except for elevated HbA1c; elevated anti-thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibodies.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial CSF analysis showed mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (WBC 12/mm3, 75% lymphocytes) and markedly elevated protein (2.97 g/L); repeat LP 2 weeks later showed turbid CSF with WBC 14/mm3 (70% neutrophils), protein 3.37 g/L, and glucose 4.6 mmol/L. Initial brain MRI demonstrated right temporal cortical lesions, acute frontoparietal lacunar infarcts, microangiopathy, and cerebral atrophy; repeat MRI at 2 weeks showed diffuse pachymeningeal and leptomeningeal enhancement; third MRI at 2 months showed persistent pachymeningeal enhancement and a new left temporal convexity focal lesion without acute ischemia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Although blood and CSF bacterial cultures were negative, strongly positive serum Brucella serology (>1:1280) and a positive CSF Brucella PCR confirmed chronic neurobrucellosis presenting with parkinsonism, dementia, psychosis, and pachymeningitis. Treated with an initial 2.5-month course of oral doxycycline (100 mg BID), oral rifampin (600 mg QD), oral TMP-SMX (800/160 mg BID), and intermittent IV ceftriaxone (2 g QD), concurrent with a 1-month course of oral dexamethasone (4 mg q6h tapered over 3 weeks), followed by an additional 6-week oral course of doxycycline, rifampin, and TMP-SMX for persistent CSF hyperproteinorrachia. Repeat CSF Brucella PCR turned negative, serum titers declined to 1:640, hallucinations, rigidity, and bradykinesia resolved, limb strength improved to 4/5, and he was discharged home after a 2-month rehabilitation program.
